lessons_to_retain: A detailed prompt does not prove the generated raster obeyed exact color, transparency, palette, pose count, or frame-grid requirements.
Inspect the actual saved PNG after generation: read dimensions, color mode, alpha, color histogram, exact key-color samples, and each cell before accepting the visible preview.
A visual magenta-looking background may contain gradients or semi-transparent fringe; compare RGB samples to the exact required key and stop promotion on mismatch.
Keep authored pose IDs and the source-pose count distinct from cell dimensions, tiles, VDP objects, and animation timing.

Review all frames in temporal order at native size and nearest-neighbor 4x; explicitly trace face, both hands, shoulder-elbow-wrist chain, weapon grip, full weapon endpoints, baseline, silhouette, and material shadow flow.
Lock identity and morphology to the owner-approved source. Reuse the clean v10 color grouping as a treatment reference only; do not copy its movement or carry its earlier edge defects forward.

Keep every generated version in review_drafts with an immutable hash and prompt/source lineage. A detected defect makes that version a review-only candidate; do not place it in res/, a conversion proof, or a ROM.
An approved move design authorizes sequential art production only. It does not approve generated pixels, frame data, hitboxes, palette conversion, hardware budgets, or runtime behavior.

Record the planned effect of at least seven animation principles against exact pose IDs and justify the rest; after drawing, verify those effects in the actual sequence rather than relying on prompt language.

Transparent-background generation can return semi-transparent pixels across the character and halo; inspect the alpha histogram and require alpha exactly 0/255 before cutout, indexed conversion, or promotion. A transparent preview is not proof of a clean binary sprite mask.
A black-looking RGB preview is not an exact key: measure exact-key pixels, near-black counts, mode and unique-color histogram; do not infer a clean cutout from display appearance.
Requesting transparent_background=true can produce glow and partial alpha rather than a binary mask; require alpha exactly 0/255 and inspect the saved PNG before accepting it.
